scope: Common Compute/Graph native input ownership lookup; no model/provider branch, public API change or GPU math change
result: A guarded uncached binding-preparation pass collects nonexclusive owned-read record ordinals once in original order; each lookup retains the original live view/resource/handle/range check. Scope exit/failure clears ordinals.

source.status: product sources frozen; no build/GPU by owner
source.private_protocol_changed: resource_episode.h: collect/clear call-scoped ordinal span; sole input_lease caller takes that span, no old overload or active cache

implementation.conclusion: Guarded eligible record membership is stable for the uncached binding-preparation call. No prior permission or hit/miss result is reused.

guard_proof.fact: Exactly two prepare_invocation_bindings callers: RegionAccess::visit_bound and Invocation::prepare_replay. Both successfully begin_preparation then hold PreparationScope until returning. begin_preparation first checks resource_control_ready, then publishes preparation_uses=1; release is RAII.

Ordinary bind/reset and prepare_resources check resource_control_ready; owned/configuration/projected/reserve_reads/take_write entry points first require_resources, which calls the same guard. preparation_uses !=0 returns Unavailable before altering bindings, read/write handles, exclusivity, anonymous page records or capacity. Public control is externally serialized; native hooks receive const input values/leases, not writable ResourceEpisode records.

project_generated_output updates native_values, readable, bound and the separate external-alias projection index. It never grows ResourceEpisode.bindings or mutates its read/exclusive fields. New native output values still pass the original descriptor/resource/alignment checks.

read.valid only tests block_ nonnull, not asynchronous readiness. Current binding handle membership cannot change through legal guarded mutation; another caller dropping a ReadLease copy does not edit these handles. Every lookup still checks the actual exclusive/read handle, calls live read.view and verifies actual resource/handle/offset/span. No lease is retained by ordinal scratch.

The result accessor can publish an output writer to a reader after success; such records remain exclusive and excluded. An uncached binding episode has outputs_ready withdrawn by existing invalidation, and a cached pass returns through the old seal-only branch before collect. This is not a claim that all LeaseBlock readiness or refcounts stay immutable.

implementation.single_path: collect returns span<const uint32_t> into ResourceEpisode integer scratch; sole private input_lease caller passes it explicitly. No scope-outside fallback, active bool, compatible overload, added executor or global cache.
implementation.selection: Ascending original binding ordinals with !exclusive && read.valid only. Valid zero-byte views and anonymous projected guards are included. Original first covering lease order and original live matching/return body are preserved.
implementation.scope: After original complete input/output validation and before the original step pass, collect once. Existing util::ScopeGuard clears logical scratch length on success, native hook/projection/align/seal failure and early returns. Reset also clears length. Cached bindings_prepared still follows its unchanged seal path.
implementation.capacity: prepare_resources reserves scratch with actual bindings.capacity using the original ResourceEpisode allocator. reserve_reads grows it beside the binding vector, including the existing-capacity early branch so a prior partial reserve can be repaired. collect requires guarded preparation, indexable binding count and pre-reserved capacity>=bindings.size. It never reserve/allocate/sort while collecting or looking up; uint32 push cannot grow after that bound.
implementation.OOM: New cold allocation uses the same budget-aware allocator. Initial candidate construction unwinds via existing ResourceEpisodeOwner. reserve_reads failures retain owned metadata capacity as the original vector-reserve path already allowed, without publishing new lease/use capacity; retry repairs it. Any insufficient scratch returns ResourceExhausted before hook use, with no unchecked push or accepted user work.
implementation.runtime_bound: O(B+P*R) visits for B bindings, P native input lookups, R eligible records. For R approximately B worst case remains O(P*B) plus one B collection; only repeated traversal of bindings without a read handle is removed. No performance claim.

probe_basis.root_reported: Accepted isolated counter run:64 vectors equal, B102/R1,680 lookups per decode and69360 original record visits;2217072 total visits. This owner did not run it or infer time savings from counter-instrumented duration.

minimal_test_boundaries: Original fixed-record first covering read despite reverse public bind order and overlapping broad/narrow read views.
Actual same-address ownership withdrawal -> no covering lease, then new owner; native prepare failure followed by retry rebuilds scratch.
Hook reentrant bind/reset/prepare_resources rejects before mutation; no membership invalidation cache needed.
Valid zero-byte read subview at allocation end remains eligible and exactrange live check remains.
Reuse existing exclusive writer/upgradeable reader and anonymous projected page guards plus metadata allocation-failure reset/retry neighbors; no full matrix.
implementation.test_owner: bf16_fusion_review owns region_provider_test.cc; no test edits/build/GPU by this product owner
implementation.owner_refresh: Root refreshed resources.cc (private definition) and executable.cc (the sole private input_lease caller). The private header changes declarations/signature only, with no changed inline definition or visible owner/PlanState/InvocationState layout; unrelated includers do not need an artificial rebuild for this focused increment. Native and SDK objects are reused.
not_claimed: No build, test, GPU, new timing or throughput gain by this owner.
No cached permissions/readiness/lookup hits or lease ownership across binding episodes.

independent_review.status: Read-only source review: no blocking defect found. No build or runtime performed by this reviewer.

findings.conclusion: Both prepare_invocation_bindings entry points own PreparationScope after begin_preparation. Candidate ordinals are a local span, not stored with native ports. Binding/reset/configuration/projected/reserve/write-take mutations route through resource_control_ready/require_resources; generated outputs change readable/native_values/bound, not ResourceEpisode bindings. This uses the existing same-Invocation thread-compatibility contract, not a new concurrent mutation guarantee.

findings.topic: Same live permission and range semantics
findings.conclusion: Collector preserves all original binding ordinals in order when !exclusive && read.valid(); valid is block_ != nullptr and does not discard size0. Each selected candidate still rechecks exclusive, read.valid, current view success, resource/native handle and subtraction-based containment. The old first-covering body is unchanged. Anonymous projected guard suffixes remain in the same scan; exclusive published writers remain excluded.

Capacity error clears candidates before returning; all returns after successful collection are covered by ScopeGuard, including alias validation, native hook, generated projection and seal errors. Successful/failed cached-seal and incomplete-binding early exits precede collection and retain no prior scratch. Reset defensively clears it again; retry rebuilds from current bindings.

findings.topic: Cold allocator capacity and partial reserve
findings.conclusion: The candidate vector uses the episode supplied allocator. Initial capacity is reserved in the transactional candidate ResourceEpisode before publication; exception destroys the unpublished episode. reserve_reads reserves candidate capacity after bindings capacity and before committing uses/reserved_reads. A failed reserve may retain enlarged vector capacity, but does not publish new lease permissions or replace old uses; retry repairs candidate capacity even for extra<=reserved_reads. Collection verifies capacity>=bindings.size, and pushes at most that many uint32 values, so collection performs no allocation.

limitations: Worst case R=B: filtering changes repeated eligibility checks from O(P*B) to O(B+P*R), not a global linear-time or measured-latency guarantee.
OOM/capacity and no-allocation claims above are static control-flow/allocator checks, not a new fault-injection or allocation-counter run.
New tests and original exclusive/projected/result neighbours require the root actual build/run; this review does not label them passed.
independent_review.changes_by_reviewer: None in product, tests, build recipes or runtime.

design.complexity: O(B+P*R) record visits for B bindings/P queries/R eligible reads; worst R=B remains O(P*B). No permission/readiness/match cache and no lease retained by the integer scratch.
design.allocation: Original ResourceEpisode allocator and cold prepare_resources/reserve_reads capacity; collection checks capacity and never grows it. No new device buffer or executor; this is not a global no-allocation claim.

actual_build.private_header_boundary: Only declarations/private lookup signature changed; sole protocol caller and definition refreshed. No inline body or visible owner/PlanState/InvocationState layout change requiring unrelated consumers to refresh.
